en.title: Adjacent Swaps to Put the Lightest First and the Heaviest Last
en.description:
Blocks of distinct weights are arranged in an array, and each operation swaps two adjacent blocks. The lightest block must end up first and the heaviest last; the middle does not need to be sorted. Find the minimum number of swaps.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the distinct weights. 2≤n≤100000, 1≤weight≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 3 and 1. In the second example the two extremes cross, and that step must not be counted twice.
hints: Add the index l of the lightest block and the distance n−1−r of the heaviest block from the end; if l>r the two cross, so subtract 1.
